title: CBP makes electronic refunds the default
summary: CBP's interim final rule took effect February 6, 2026. Subject to limited exceptions, CBP now issues all refunds electronically.

title: IEEPA tariffs ended (Executive Order 14389)
summary: The additional IEEPA ad valorem duties are no longer in effect and, as soon as practicable, are no longer to be collected. The order does not affect other duties, such as Section 232 and Section 301 duties.

title: De minimis suspension continued for all countries (Executive Order 14388)
summary: Except for articles covered by 50 U.S.C. 1702(b), the de minimis exemption stays unavailable regardless of value, country of origin, transport mode or entry method, for goods entered on or after February 24, 2026.

title: Temporary 10% import surcharge under Section 122 (Proclamation 11012)
summary: A 10% ad valorem surcharge under section 122 applies from February 24, 2026 for 150 days, through 12:01 a.m. EDT on July 24, 2026, unless extended by an Act of Congress.

title: Steel, aluminum and copper duties now apply to full value (Proclamation 11021)
summary: For goods entered on or after April 6, 2026, Section 232 metals duties apply to the full customs value of the product, regardless of metal content.

title: Executive Order 14411 on customs enforcement and importers of record
summary: The order directs a ban on informal entry by foreign importers of record. It also directs that, within 180 days, all importers of record be required to keep good standing with CBP, and those not in good standing may not import.

title: CBP indefinitely suspends de minimis for non-postal shipments
summary: CBP's suspension of de minimis for non-postal shipments took effect June 24, 2026. CBP names Entry Type 11 as the main informal entry method for these shipments.

title: CBP suspends de minimis for mail and creates a postal informal entry
summary: The postal rule took effect July 24, 2026 (its 19 CFR 145.31 suspension took effect June 24). Outside a delayed compliance period, the new postal informal entry covers mail shipments valued at $2,500 or less that are classifiable in HTSUS chapters 1-97.

title: CBP seeks comment on IEEPA court-ordered refund worksheet
summary: CBP says the worksheet is needed to handle the volume of tariff refunds expected in the time the Court of International Trade requires. Comments were due by September 8, 2026.

agency: Office of the U.S. Trade Representative
title: New Section 301 tariffs tied to forced-labor import bans
summary: The tariffs apply to goods entered on or after 12:01 a.m. ET on July 24, 2026. The rate is 12.5% for investigated economies not otherwise listed and for products of China, except as the annexes provide.

title: CBP sets customs user fees for FY2027
summary: New customs user fee amounts are required as of October 1, 2026. The MPF minimum is $34.58 and the maximum is $670.86.

title: CBP announces enhanced enforcement of importer of record data accuracy
summary: Enhanced enforcement started September 18, 2026. CBP warns that inaccurate importer of record information may lead to immediate voiding of IOR numbers.

title: CBP weighs new supply chain disclosures for imports
summary: CBP is considering amending its regulations to get more visibility into the supply chains of imported goods. Comments are due December 1, 2026.

agency: Office of the U.S. Trade Representative
title: China Section 301 tariffs continue after their 2026 anniversary dates
summary: USTR determined that the 2018 China Section 301 actions did not terminate at their 2026 anniversaries and remain in effect.

title: CBP proposes new low-value shipment entry rules
summary: The proposal would create entry type 13 for mail shipments of $2,500 or less and require a basic importation and entry bond for entry type 11 and 13 filers. Comments are due December 7, 2026.

title: New requirements for foreign importers of record
summary: CBP's interim final rule sets new requirements for foreign importers of record when making entry. It takes effect January 5, 2027.
